issues: meaning_changed: "असत्यम्, यानी असत्य। वे संसार को असत्य और बिना आधार का बताते हैं, जिसका अर्थ है कि उन्होंने पहले ही तय कर लिया है कि किसी भी कर्म का कोई नैतिक आधार नहीं है।" (The word meaning of 'asatyam' is 'untrue', which is supported. However, the notice adds the unsupported inference that 'untrue' means 'without foundation' (binna aadhar), which is actually the meaning of 'apratishtham'. It also adds an unsupported motive that they have 'already decided' there is no moral ground for any action.)

borrowed: "Notice: असत्यम्, यानी असत्य। वे संसार को असत्य कहते हैं, जिससे वे किसी भी कर्म का नैतिक आधार ही नहीं मानते।" (The notice presents the content of the previous verse (verse 7), which describes people with a shadowed nature who have no purity, noble conduct, or truthfulness. The notice incorrectly attributes this description of lacking moral ground to the asuric worldview of verse 8, which specifically focuses on the world being 'asatyam' (unreal) and without a ruling lord.)

borrowed: "यही विचार रखकर, नष्ट बुद्धि वाले लोग संसार को नष्ट करने के लिए ही उत्पन्न होते हैं।" (This is the Hindi translation of the NEXT verse (verse 9), not this verse (verse 8). The Hindi 'next' field incorrectly presents the content of the following verse as if it were the translation of this verse.)
